Minor damage to Blue Hill Fair building after weed-burning accident

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 1:32
Instaread
By Ben Pinette
on July 31, 2026

BY LILY FROST
FacebookXMessengerCopy LinkMessageEmailShare

Fire trucks report to the scene just outside the Charlote’s Web exhibit building on the Blue Hill Fairgrounds. (By Lily Frost)

BLUE HILL—The Blue Hill Fair had a close call—and frightening scare—on Friday, July 31, just over a month away from opening day of the annual event.

Minor damage from the fire to the exterior wall of the Pulling Grandstand. (Courtesy of Blue Hill Fire Department)

At 7:55 a.m., the Blue Hill Fire Department received a call reporting a fire in the Exhibition Hall Building on the fairgrounds. When crews arrived, they found that the flames were actually closer to the Pulling Building, home to the popular Charlotte’s Web Exhibit, which was first opened four years ago.

David Gray, President of the board of directors of the Blue Hill Fair, said, “When I heard the call it sounded like it was the grandstand, but thankfully it wasn’t.” Gray said the fire, which caused very minor damage to one of the outbuildings, started when “a workman was burning weeds with a propane burner along the side of the building and got too close. He had a fire extinguisher and got the fire subdued, then the fire department put it out completely.”

Gray added, “Very minor damage, a little siding and some studs.”

Blue Hill Fire Department Chief John Chapman said that fire departments from Blue Hill, Brooksville, Brooklin, Penobscot, and Sedgwick were called in. The fire was on the exterior wall of the Pulling Grandstand and was confirmed by the department to be caused by burning grass nearby.

An official statement released by Blue Hill Fair echoed a similar message, thanking first responders and assuring the public that the damage was minimal. The fair will be ready to be enjoyed come September 3.
